judgments.reason: Title and abstract describe the same multi-expert seizure annotation SEEG dataset (UPenn and CHOP, spontaneous and stimulation-induced seizures) with matching authors, though the preprint counts (83 seizures, 32 patients) differ from the dataset's 78 and 29.
judgments.paper_title: Multi-expert consensus annotations of spontaneous and stimulation-induced seizures in stereotactic EEG

judgments.reason: Same title and authors as the dataset (Multi-Expert Seizure Annotation, Ojemann et al.); the Pennsieve Discover record is the original deposit of the same data that NEMAR redistributes.
MNE-BIDS is a software tool for organizing electrophysiology data into BIDS, used in dataset formatting, not a paper describing this seizure annotation dataset.
judgments.paper_title: MNE-BIDS: Organizing electrophysiological data into the BIDS format and facilitating their analysis
judgments.paper_venue: The Journal of Open Source Software

judgments.reason: iEEG-BIDS is a specification for organizing intracranial EEG data, which this BIDS-formatted SEEG dataset follows. It does not describe this dataset itself.
judgments.paper_title: iEEG-BIDS, extending the Brain Imaging Data Structure specification to human intracranial electrophysiology
